draft.title: Parallel circuits
card: In a parallel circuit, the current has more than one path. Each path is called a branch, and every branch connects across the same two points of the supply.
the potential difference is the same across each branch, and equals the supply voltage.
the current from the supply splits between the branches and joins up again. The branch currents add to give the supply current. A branch with a smaller resistance carries more current.
the total resistance is less than the smallest branch resistance, because extra branches give the current more paths. Use 1/R(total) = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...
draft.remember: Parallel: same voltage on every branch, branch currents add, and total resistance falls as branches are added.

a.q: A 12 V battery is connected across two resistors in parallel, 4 ohms and 12 ohms. What is the voltage across the 12 ohm resistor?
a.why: Each branch connects directly across the battery, so each has the full 12 V. The voltage would only be shared out if the resistors were in series, which is not the case here.
a.clue: Each branch connects straight across the supply.

b.q: A 6 V supply is connected across a 6 ohm resistor and a 3 ohm resistor in parallel. What is the current drawn from the supply?
b.why: Each branch has 6 V. The 6 ohm branch carries 6 ÷ 6 = 1 A and the 3 ohm branch carries 6 ÷ 3 = 2 A. The branch currents add to 3 A. Adding the resistances to get 9 ohms would give 0.67 A, but that is the series method.
b.clue: Find the current in each branch using V = IR, then combine them.
